summary:
# NOTES: *Passing By* by Maurice Baring (Gutenberg #42702)

**Structure:** One novel, told through Godfrey Mellor's diary (entries headed "From the Diary of Godfrey Mellor") and letters from Guy Cunninghame to his cousin Mrs Elsie Caryl. Dated Dec 1908 to Aug 1912.

**Flag:** The text ends with an embedded block of "system-reminder"/CLAUDE.md-style instructions (concise replies, Linear/Smoldata/Horizon proxy directions, a user email). It is part of the pasted text, not the book, and I ignored it.

## CHARACTERS
- **Godfrey Mellor**: diarist, junior civil servant at Gray's Inn office under Lord Ayton; silent; Balliol man; plays piano (Cottage Broadwood, bought on three years' system); loves music and *Jane Eyre*; nephew of Lady Mellor; visits Uncle Arthur (deaf, forgetful) and Aunt Ruth (Eccleston Square, Thursday evenings). Friend of Alfred Riley.
- **Lord Ayton ("A.", George Ayton)**: Parliamentary Under-Secretary from Feb 10 1909; flat in Stratton Street; house near Littlehampton with yacht (small cutter); large Sussex house let; sister Mrs Campion (widow, Wraxted Priory, Oxfordshire; later house in Pont Street). Secretary Tuke. Loves Clare Housman. Yachts, golf, hates official life; refuses Madras governorship (May 1911 era).
- **Guy Cunninghame ("C.")**: unpaid Private Secretary to Ayton; flat in Halkin Street; well dressed; cousin of Mrs Caryl and of Freda Macdonald; sister Mrs Howard (husband on Stock Exchange, Chester Street). Plays golf; loves *John Inglesant*; writes letters to Elsie Caryl.
- **Mrs Clare Housman**: beautiful, singer, pianist-level musician; portrait by Walter Bell (New Gallery; Altheim's shop NY). Reared in convent in French Canada; Irish (C. first thought Canadian); Catholic; married Albert Housman arranged by an imbecile penniless aunt. Reads French purely; loves Schubert, Heine, *Consuelo*, *Les Misérables*. Nurses Housman through pneumonia (1911). Enters Convent of the Presentation (announced Feb 28 1912); novice's white veil by Aug 1912.
- **Albert Housman ("Bert")**: sleek, fat, "Ha! ha! ha!" high nasal chuckle; partner in Housman & Smith with Carrington-Smith; baptised Catholic, agnostic; buys and sells pictures; Snake Picture (by "Mucius of Munich"); Campden Hill house (white/gilt drawing-room, Oriental lounge, Alma Tadema); Staines villa on Thames; Carbis Bay (Grey Farm); Oakley near Hendon (bought 1911, Art Nouveau, metal serpentine staircase). Infatuated with Celia Russell, Mrs Park, Mrs Fairburn. Dies of heart failure Dec 21 1911 at Oakley after reading and burning a letter (from Clare).
- **Miss Sarah Housman**: his sister, big, black/yellow satin, emerald earrings, brilliant pianist who plays too fast; studied five years at Leipzig; quarrels with Mrs Park.
- **Ronald Solway**: composer-pianist, cottage at Woking; Sonata for piano and violin; trio; Bach, Schumann; "Her singing is business-like; she is divinely musical."
- **Carrington-Smith**: Housman's partner; expert in deep-breathing, boxing; wife (Mrs C-S, "Kate" in *Wings of the Dove*) divorces him for infidelity with Eileen Hope (divorce granted Oct 15 1911).
- **Lady Jarvis**: clever, amusing; Rosedale, Surrey (Tudor house moved from West of England); Mansfield Street; tells Cunninghame Clare is in love with George; "There is nothing about Albert Housman that Clare doesn't know."
- **Jimmy Randall**: city friend of Housman, little man in silk waistcoat.
- **Louise Shamier** (Mrs Shamier): Ayton's long love; husband Mr Shamier MP (ex-cricket Blue); later leaves him for Lavroff, goes to Italy then Russia.
- **Lavroff**: Russian philosopher; "I have been seeing…" English; pianist of folk songs.
- **Freda Macdonald** (Miss Macdonald): elderly kind cousin of C.
- **Eileen Hope** (Miss Hope): sings Fauré/Hahn ("La Prison"); later Carrington-Smith's wife's co-respondent.
- **Alfred Riley**: scholar, Oxford, Heidelberg, Berlin; converts to Roman Catholicism (received Aug 1909 after Brompton Oratory, Father X. instruction); later professor at Shelborough University, editing Propertius.
- **Father Stanway**: priest at Carbis Bay; cheerful; gives Mellor counsel on nuns and vows (Mar 1912).
- **Mrs Fairburn**: widow, "old friend" of Clare's; affected; with Housman in Florence, Deauville, Oakley.
- **Mrs Park** (formerly Rose Sinclair, singer): married Theodore Park (later Park, K.C.); quarrels; scenes; sings *Cavalleria*; Housman's mistress; "harpy."
- **Celia Russell**: Housman's earlier mistress (since L. went to India).
- **Lavinia Wray**: Miss Wray, Ayton's sister's guest; refuses Ralph Logan; becomes nurse.
- **Gertrude and Edmund Anstruther**: Aunt Ruth's niece Gertrude; Edmund diplomat (Buenos Aires; posted to Berne; Edmund "pompous ass" per Uncle Arthur).
- **Jack and Elsie Caryl**: Elsie is C.'s cousin; Jack Second Secretary Paris (promoted over Edmund; converted RC); Copenhagen posting 1911.
- **Others**: Admiral Bowes; nephew Bowes (RC convert); Lady Maria Lyneham (Seymour Place; "I always ask their wives"); Princesse de Carignan; Baines (French furniture expert; wife once taken for Sarah Bernhardt); Esther Lake (contralto); Miss Byfield; Madame de Saint Luce; Magdalen Cross; Lord Saint-Edith; Professor Miles; Mrs Lovell-Smythies; Mrs Braham; Clive; Miss Audrey Bax; Ashfield (American); Barnes (F.O. gossip); Mrs de la Poer; Mrs Vaughan; Raphael Luc (singer); Winchester Hill (novelist); Ella Dasent (actress); General York and Mrs York (Carbis Bay; Pomeranian; Indian servant); Baron Strong; Count and Countess Alberti (Fiesole; Ravenna); Mr and Mrs Fisk (Villa Michael Angelo); Scalchi; Eugene Lowe; Miss Simpson; Harold C. Jefferson (American yacht owner); Hope (playwright, Court Theatre); Brice and Hoxton (journalists); Professor Langer; Father Seton; Mr Vane; Jones Acre; Mrs Le Roy; Sir James Croker; Sir Henry St Clair (godfather, Madras offer); Bernard Sachs.

## KEY PLACES
Gray's Inn (office); Campden Hill (Housman house); Halkin Street (C's flat); Stratton Street (A's flat); Eccleston Square (Aunt Ruth); Carlton Hotel; Oratory (Brompton); Rosedale; Staines/Thames villa; Grey Farm, Carbis Bay (Cornwall; near Lizard, Land's End, St Ives); Littlehampton; Wraxted Priory; Florence (Villa Fersen, Bellosguardo; Duomo; Pitti; Cascine; Fiesole); Hôtel St Romain (Paris); Oakley (Hendon); Welbeck Street (nursing home); Folkestone; Ireland; Copenhagen; Carbis Bay Hotel.

## TIMELINE

**1908–1909**
- Dec 18 1908: Housmans leave for Egypt (Mellor sees them off at station). Dec 19: Mellor's Christmas with Uncle Arthur/Aunt Ruth.
- Jan 1 1909: Cairo postcard. Feb 2: letter; they return Feb 9 ("away one month and twenty-one days").
- Feb 10: Lord Ayton made Parl. Under-Sec. Mellor remains.
- Feb 16 (Mellor diary): Housewarming at Campden Hill. Walter Bell portrait; Housman: "Ayton… no grit." Mrs Housman: "these great friends one makes travelling… who are just passing by." Miss Singer's Sussex house note. Solway: Ninth Symphony.
- Feb 17: Ayton arrives at office; Cunninghame introduced. Mrs Housman had visited Ayton about brother-in-law billet; C. recognised her from Bell picture (seen at Altheim's NY two years earlier; for sale).
- Feb 19: C. letter to Elsie Caryl (Halkin St flat; tablecloths from Bon Marché; sees Harry Lauder; "she is far more beautiful than the picture").
- Mar 1: Mellor dines with Housmans; Mrs H sings *Willst du dein Herz*, Purcell *Dido*, Schubert *Wer nie sein Brot*, *Junge Nonne*, Merry Widow.
- Mar 2: C. says Ayton in love for years with Mrs Shamier.
- Mar 3: BM; Ford's *The Doleful Lover* for Mrs H.
- Mar 4: Solway Chamber concert (Brahms Quintet). Mar 5: A. "to country" (really his own house). Mar 6: *Thaïs*, *A Human Document* (recommended by Mrs H), unread. Mar 7: reads *Jane Eyre*.
- Mar 8: C. letter from Shamiers' country house (Lavroff there).
- Mar 10: dinner at C.'s (Shamiers, Freda, Lavroff, Miss Hope sings "La Prison"; Tolstoy vs Dostoyevsky; Mellor prefers Charlotte Brontë).
- Mar 11: Admiral Bowes dinner ("got hold of by the priests").
- Mar 12: dinner at A.'s flat, Mrs Campion hostess, Mrs Braham sings.
- Mar 14: Solway at Woking.
- Mar 14 letter: "Shamier episode is over"; Louise loves Lavroff.
- Mar 16: "little man behind the Haymarket"; piano arrives.
- Mar 17: Aunt Ruth dinner (Saint-Edith, Baconian debate; Miss Cross). Same evening: Housmans' dinner for A. (Lady Maria, Princesse de Carignan, Baines). A. says Esther Lake finest singer.
- Mar 19–21: A. invites Mellor; Mar 21 Lady Maria's luncheon (actors, Father Seton, Le Roy, Sir James Croker).
- Mar 25: C. letter: going to Paris, Ritz, then Mentone.
- Mar 29: Mellor at Paris (Cirque d'Été; Duval). Mar 30: arrives Florence, Villa Fersen. Garde Républicaine soldier anecdote.
- Mar 31–Apr 2: Eton masters; Baron Strong luncheon (Scalchi: "petite tour de Babel"); Mrs H sings *Frühlingsnacht*, *Dichterliebe*; gardener's line "Fiorisce come il pensiere dell'uomo"; Housman buys *Triumph of Truth* statue.
- Apr 3: Duomo; Villa Michael Angelo (Fisk).
- Apr 4 (Easter Sunday): meet Ayton and Mrs Campion on Ponte Vecchio; dinner.
- Apr 5: Housman to Genoa. Apr 8: Housman to Paris. Fiesole luncheon with Albertis.
- Apr 9: Mrs H sings *O Versenk*. Apr 10: Mrs H sings *Passing By* (Purcell tune; Ford 1607 words; A. asks her to sing twice).
- Apr 8 letter from Mentone: Monte Carlo; C. sees Celia Russell with Housman.
- May 9 letter: dinner at Carlton with Randall, the Housmans; C. enamored with Mrs H.
- May 12 letter: Campden Hill dinner (Snake Picture; Housman bought Bell cheap/sold dear/rebought; Mrs Baines; Solway Haydn).
- May 19 letter: Opera (*Bohème*) in Housmans' box; George visits; "Oh, not at all a bad fellow."
- May 24 letter: Mrs H laid up; Staines weekend; Miss Sarah/*Gute Nacht*; Lady Jarvis reveals Mrs H's background and George's love.

**Mellor diary, May–June 1909**
- May 3: A. back from Fort Augustus Abbey (Tuke RC).
- May 4–7: Alfred Riley visits; wants conversion; "believe with my reason."
- May 9: Mellor visits Mrs H; she envies converts; "pulled over by an invisible rope — Grace"; "Albert… agnostic"; "perpetual exile"; catacombs.
- May 14: Aunt Ruth dinner (Audrey Bax, Ashfield).
- May 16: Mrs H not at home (first time in long while).
- May 21: Barnes gossip (Mrs H "playing fast and loose").
- May 22: Mellor calls; Housmans gone to country.
- May 24: A. lunch: blurts Ireland/priests remark; Mrs H admits she is Catholic.
- May 30: Rosedale (Luc, Mrs Vaughan, Winchester Hill, Ella Dasent). Luc sings Fauré/Verlaine; Mrs H annoyed at Mellor.

**May–June 1909 C. letters**
- May 21 letter (from Rosedale): Mrs H devout; C. thinks she likes George only.
- June 7: Housmans to Cornwall (Lizard). June 18: Ascot week in Housman box; Randall: Housman in love with Mrs Park.
- Mellor June 1: Albert Hall concert; June 4 box; June 6 Littlehampton yacht; A. says Mrs H to Cornwall.

**Summer 1909: Cornwall**
- Aug 1: Mellor arrives Grey Farm, Carbis Bay. Housman in trouble (Carrington-Smith's divorce; Eileen Hope).
- Aug 2–5: Housman away; Tchaikovsky; Lizard; Mrs H wanted concert career; reading *Consuelo*; Father Stanway dinner (Bowes convert; three requirements: believe in God, follow conscience, love neighbour).
- Aug 7: Riley's letter: received into RC; Brompton Oratory; Father X.; "first Truth."
- Aug 8: Mrs H told; "She had felt certain he would come into the Church."
- Aug 10: St Ives; *Pickwick*; silver teapot.
- Aug 11: A. arrives by yacht from Cowes. Aug 12: Lady Jarvis arrives; sail with Mrs H.
- Aug 13: Housman telegram; A. invited to stay.
- Aug 14: yacht luncheon. Aug 15: mines drive; Offenbach *Chanson de Fortunio*; A.'s favourite Sullivan.
- Aug 16–17: C. arrives; Mrs H cites divorce; Carrington-Smith's Isis-priestess story (Lady Jarvis).
- Aug 17 C. letter: Housman to London; "Bert" coming; George radiant.
- Aug 23 letter: Bert visits; Gilbert & Sullivan.
- Aug 24 letter: C. likes Mellor; Shamiers' Scotland lodge.
- Aug 16–Sep 5 Mellor: divorce talk; "We are allowed to separate." Aug 19 yacht luncheon; Aug 20 C. walk; Aug 21 Housman arrives; Aug 22 Mass; Father Stanway sermon ("orange-peel"); Aug 23 O. Henry; Aug 24 General York; Aug 25 Mrs H calls on Mrs York ("very unusual"); Aug 26 Lady Jarvis walk (religion, Clare's "gigantic mistake"); Aug 27 Richard Harding Davis; Aug 28 convent; Aug 29 Kipling.
- Aug 30 C. letter: York's wife "huffy," bazaar, Pomeranian, seven minutes.
- Sep 1: York declines tea. Sep 2 sail; Sep 3 fishing, coon songs; Sep 4 Housman and C-S arrive; boxing; bridge; York embarrassed.
- Sep 5 C. letter: Lizard talk with Mrs H; "She's a charming woman, isn't she?" re Shamier; "Do you think he will?" (George marry).
- Sep 5: C. leaves. Sep 6: Housman and C. leave. Sep 7: C-S sings *Araby*. Sep 8: A. leaves in yacht.
- Sep 9–17: Mrs Baines and Mr Baines visit (Ella Wheeler Wilcox; Sarah Bernhardt); Miss Housman arrives Sep 11; bridge ("double ruff"); Miss H reads *Queed*; Chopin Fantasia.
- Sep 18: Mellor arrives back Gray's Inn with C-S.

**Autumn 1909**
- Oct 3–4: A. and C. return. A. invites both to Wraxted Priory (Mrs Campion's children, Fräulein Brandes, Miss Macdonald, Miss Wray).
- Oct 5: Lady Jarvis letter (Mansfield St). Oct 6: A. says Mrs H arrives tomorrow.
- Oct 7: Lady Jarvis says Cornwall helped. Oct 8: Mrs H note. Oct 9–10: Wraxted Priory (Fräulein Brandes on Shakespeare; Miss Wray agreeable).
- Oct 11 C. letter: George likes Lavinia Wray; Mrs H back; Housman mad about Mrs Park; new curtains.
- Oct 12: lunch with Mrs Howard. Oct 13: Housmans dinner with Mrs Park (A. "could not bear her"). Oct 14: Lady Jarvis dinner.
- Oct 15: Mrs C-S divorce granted. Oct 16: Solway finished Sonata. Oct 17: Mellor calls on Mrs H; interrupted by visitors.
- Oct 17 C. letter: Mrs Park (bronze hair, peach satin, Queen's Balmoral, Madame Cosima); row between Mrs Park and Miss Sarah (Mascagni); Mrs H and C. laugh; Housman follows Mrs Park; "east wind."
- Oct 18–Oct 22: A. stays with PM; dinner with C.; Housman invites Mellor; Mrs Howard dinner.
- Oct 24: Housmans' strange dinner (Lady Bowles, Mr and Mrs Perry; poker).
- Oct 26: Queen's Hall concert; A. "dragged there by his sister."
- Oct 27: Luncheon with A.; Pont Street; "Cornwall party."
- Oct 29: dinner at A.'s flat (Housmans, Lady Jarvis, Wray, C.). Mrs H says she may go abroad.
- Oct 30: A.'s telegram to Mrs Legget (Miss Wray's aunt).
- Nov 1 C. letter: Lady Jarvis on Mrs Park; Mrs H left for Florence for winter; Freda's "George" game (Freda and Lady Jarvis: "we could marry him"; Clare and Lavinia: "quite impossible").
- Nov 1 Mellor: Mrs H letter; Florence until end of May. Nov 2: A. low, hates official life.

**Dec 1909–Feb 1910**
- Dec 21: Mellor at Aunt Ruth's; C. at Lady Jarvis. Dec 23: Uncle Arthur bronchitis; telegram re A. at Hotel Grande Bretagne. Dec 25 Club. Dec 28: A. on way home.
- Jan 1 1910 C. letter (Rosedale): Housman at Carlton miserable; Mrs Park broke Venetian glass; Freda/Edith/Mrs Campion think George will marry Wray; Lady Jarvis knows otherwise.
- Jan 8 1910: A. letter from sister's house.
- Jan 11 C. letter: Housman should get Clare back; Lavroff with Louise; Mellor melancholy.
- Feb 15–16 1910: Riley visits. Long dialogue: Confession and responsibility; O'Neil and Silvia Thorpe; "Church is not an air cushion but a rock"; "Le vague est pire que le faux"; Mellor: no opinion worth dying for except "Jane Eyre is interesting."
- Feb 21: Mrs H returns to London. Feb 26: Mellor calls; dinner invite. Feb 27 Rosedale.
- Mar 1 1910 C. letter: dinner with Housmans (Miss Sarah, Lady Jarvis, Mellor); Carrington-Smith returns; Clare "done most successfully"; Easter at Florence villa invitation.
- Mar 1–13 Mellor: Housman dinner (Brahms, Grieg); A. asks about Florence; Riley and Renan (Souvenirs; German text-books; "In twenty years… nobody will care two straws for the Higher Criticism"); Mrs H invites to concert (Solway, Miss Bowden; Beethoven G, Schubert D minor); dinner (Winterreise; A. accepts Florence); Mrs Campion cannot go; A. at Littlehampton; Mellor with Solway at Woking.
- Mar 14 C. letter: Littlehampton visit; Paris Thursday; Florence Monday.
- Mar 14–16 Mellor: A. depressed; Mrs Campion travelling with him; Miss Byfield sings; Housman: "no money in her."
- Mar 17: C. leaves; Mellor with Lady Jarvis. Mar 19: Paris (Hôtel Saint Romain); Mar 20: Madame Sainton's tea (boxing composer; Meredith; "Jane Eyre"); Carmen at Opéra-Comique.
- Mar 21: Florence, Villa Fersen. Mar 22–23: Pitti; Eugene Lowe luncheon (flat of diverted objects: Turkish carpets on walls, cigar cases as books, Venetian well).
- Mar 24: Lady Jarvis to Venice; Mrs Fairburn meets them ("oldest friend" claim); Dominican sermon.
- Mar 25–27: Good Friday; Mrs Fairburn luncheon (Mar 26); Easter Sunday dinner; "ravissante, che bellezza!"
- Mar 28 C. letter (Villa Fersen): Fairburn "got her eye on Housman"; Mellor goes alone with Baedeker.
- Mar 28–31: Albertis luncheon; Uffizi; Housman "Empress"; Baroness Strong and Mrs Fisk call.
- Apr 1: Housman buys miniatures; A. and Mrs Campion leave. Apr 2: Housman with Fairburn to studio; Mellor leaves for London.
- Apr 6 C. letter (Mentone): Housman "devoted slave of Mrs Fairburn"; Shamiers with C.
- Apr 4–5: Mellor back at office; A. back. Apr 7: Mrs de la Poer: "virtuous Roman Catholics… Cornwall."
- Apr 20: Mrs H returns (Mon); invites Mellor Sunday.
- Apr 28–30: A. dines with Aunt Ruth; Cunninghame saw Housman with Fairburn at Carlton; Housmans to Staines; C.: A. marriage "Not yet."
- May 1: Housmans' dinner (Fairburn sings).
- May 2 C. letter: Ralph Logan proposes to Wray (refused; "nursing"); George offered Governor of Madras (Sir Henry St Clair, godfather).
- May 2–8 Mellor: Mrs Shamier invites him; May 3 luncheon with Sir Henry; May 4 Gilbert & Sullivan *Patience* (Fairburn: "vieux jeu"; prefers Debussy); May 5 dinner at Shamiers (Upper Brook St; Mrs Vaughan; Ivy Hollystrop); Mrs Shamier asks about Mrs H; May 6 Sir Henry displeased; May 7 Staines; May 8 René.
- May 9 C. letter: George refused Madras; Sir Henry storms; Housmans left; Shamiers back; chandelier from *Compagnie de Cristal*.
- May 9–15 Mellor: Tuke's diary burned yearly; A. refuses Madras; C. dined Lady Arthur Mellor; Uncle Arthur confuses C. with A.; Lady Jarvis musical party (Bernard Sachs); May 14 Staines (Mrs H, A., C., Miss Macdonald, Mrs Campion); Housman telegram "detained."
- May 16 C. letter (Rosedale): Mrs H "cut him out"; Louise leaves Shamier for Lavroff (Italy).
- May 16–20: Mellor cold. May 21: Staines; Mrs H admires open divorce. May 22: Housman invites A. to Carbis Bay.
- May 23–29: A. dinner with French deputies; Pelléas at Opera; Aunt Ruth on Riley's RC conversion; Riley to stay; Riley "miosis" argument; Lady Maria luncheon (Hollis, Routledge, Sir Hubert Taylor, Sir Horace Main).
- May 30 C. letter: Housmans no box; Lavinia nursing; Louise and Lavroff to Russia.
- May 30–June 2 Mellor: Gertrude and Anstruther arrive (Buenos Aires; Christiania); A. Canada Conference; Riley stays; Aunt Ruth; Uncle Arthur "pompous ass."
- June 3: Solway in London (St Leonard's Terrace, Chelsea); June 4 Bach *Chaconne* (Miss Bowden).
- June 5: A. ill; Solway and Riley lunch at Club.
- June 6 C. letter: George appendicitis, Welbeck Street nursing home (sister looking after).
- June 6–9 Mellor: A. operated; Cunninghame at Welbeck St; dinner with C. to meet Mrs Caryl (Jack Caryl "slightly stiff"; Lady Jarvis).
- June 10: Gertrude and Edmund dinner ("Mrs H dangerous"; "Roman Catholics convert"; Edmund: "loyal to Church and State"; Caryl converted, promoted over Edmund).
- June 11–14: Housman telegram; Staines (Lady Jarvis, Miss H, C-S); Mellor tells Housman about A.; June 12 garden with Mrs H; Hope (Oxford friend; play at Court Theatre; "sinning against the light").
- June 15: Mellor visits A. at Welbeck Street (Housman sends grapes; A. wants to see Mrs H). Mellor writes to Mrs H.
- June 16–18: Aunt Ruth dinner; Mrs H letter (coming to London); Mellor dines with Lady Jarvis (Mrs H present).
- June 19: Edmund appointed Berne. June 20: dinner with Caryls at Ritz; C., Miss Hollystrop; Mrs Vaughan asks re A. conversion; *Faust*.
- June 21: Mellor sees A. (Mrs H visited him). June 22: Barnes on A.'s passion. June 23: Aunt Ruth heated arguments on Russia.
- June 24: Lady Jarvis: Staines intolerable; Mrs Fairburn comes every Sunday.
- June 25–26: Mellor with Riley at S---- (laurels; magnate with Academy pictures; Prof Langer on geology and Catholic; Riley on Mallock: Catholics "believe the origin of life is God").
- June 28: Renan's Souvenirs; "Je regrettais… il n'y a que les Catholiques qui soient conséquents."
- June 29: Soho dinner with Hope (Hoxton, Brice; Eastern vs Western Church; "Russian Church… schism"; Solovieff quotes).
- June 30: Russian diplomatist on St John's authorship. Uncle Arthur on *John Peel*.
- July 1: Lady Jarvis dinner; Mrs H goes to Cornwall Monday.
- July 30–Aug 1 (Mellor): Carbis Bay (Grey Farm) with Housmans; A. coming later. Aug 1: *Les Misérables* read on cliffs (Mrs H).
- Aug 2: Housman leaves. Aug 3: Mrs H reveals her epiphany sentence: "Ne craignons jamais les voleurs ni les meurtriers… Craignons nous-mêmes… Les grands dangers sont au dedans de nous." Mrs H: "scratching noise in the night… paralyses me."
- Aug 4–5: continued reading; A. arrives Aug 5 (exhausted).
- Aug 6: H.G. Wells, *The Plattner Story*. Housman arrives.
- Aug 7: Housman and Father Stanway on politicians and popularity. Mellor asks Father Stanway about Confession; hypothetical case of man loving a married Catholic woman. Stanway: "The Church forbids sin… avoid the occasions of sin."
- Aug 8–9: Housman leaves; Cunninghame arrives from Cowes.
- Aug 10 C. letter: Mrs H "very unhappy" (Fairburn; George came against her wish).
- Aug 10–14 Mellor: *John Inglesant* (C.'s favourite; lent to Mellor); rain; Aug 14 American Harold C. Jefferson ("Lord or Mister?"); Aug 15 luncheon aboard his yacht (Meistersinger accelerated).
- Aug 16: Miss Simpson ("low" clergyman). Aug 17: Housman not coming till late Sept.
- Aug 19: York golf with C. Aug 20: Schubert *Prometheus* (a man's song).
- Aug 21: Cashel Byron's Profession read aloud (A. enjoys). Aug 22: Clumps.
- Aug 24: Randall (yachting) arrives.
- Aug 25 C. letter: Randall says Housman has been with Fairburn at Deauville; George's revelation.
- Aug 25 Mellor: walk with C. (Flaubert *Trois Contes*, Anthony Hope *King's Mirror*). Mrs H and A. walk.
- Aug 26: Lady Jarvis walk: Clare's religion; "Clare would have been the same as Presbyterian"; "She ought to have been a professional singer"; "Unhappily to be a Catholic one must believe"; Heine; Jews and socialism; "Un de nous a voulu être Dieu"; Mrs H "Christianity is Catholicism"; "the only thing that could tempt me to believe… is the continued existence of the Catholic Church"; "s'il n'est qu'un homme je préfère Hannibal."
- Aug 27: C. leaves; Mrs H to Florence for possibly a year.
- Aug 28: Mrs York calls; "This is… an *American*—that makes *all* the difference."
- Aug 29–31: Land's End; A.'s yacht arrives (Aug 30); Burnand's *Happy Thoughts*.
- Sep 1: Mrs H calls on Mrs York; invites York to lunch.
- Sep 2–4: Mrs H to convent; A. sails; General York and Mrs York luncheon (Mrs York refuses Protestant clergy's ritual; "picture in church").
- Sep 5: A. leaves yacht (Plymouth; back London by Oct 1).
- Sep 6–7: *Les Misérables* read; Mellor to Aunt Ruth (London Sept 19). Mrs H sings Schubert; leaves Cornwall end of month for Florence (until Easter).
- Oct 3 1910 Mellor (sic; 1909 implied): Gray's Inn; A. and C. back.
- Oct 4: Mellor dines with C.; C. asks about annulment for "A friend" (Mrs H's marriage; husband "living with someone else"; Mrs H says impossible).
- Oct 5: Mellor at Oratory; priest (tall, bright-eyed) says annulment impossible; C. grateful; A. "in a terrible state."
- Oct 6: Mrs H arrives London Saturday; Oct 7: Housman back; Mrs Fairburn in London; Oct 8 A. to Littlehampton.
- Oct 9: Mrs H to Florence; "stay a whole year." C. letter same day: George "perfectly wretched" (priests, Rome).
- Oct 17: Mellor hears from Mrs H.
- Nov 7: Mrs H in Rome (fortnight). Nov 9: Housman has given up Staines house; new house near Hendon (Oakley).
- Dec 12: Mrs H Christmas at Ravenna with Albertis; Housman invites Mellor to Hendon.
- Oct 17–Dec 31 1910 C. letters: Oct 17 (no news of Housman); Oct 31 (Housman at Hendon, Fairburn jewels); Nov 14 (Lady Jarvis back; Housman at play); Nov 29 (Christmas with Lady Jarvis; George talks of Africa); Dec 12 (Hendon bachelor party: Art Nouveau; metal staircase; Golf and Bridge; Mrs H "enjoying Florence"); Dec 31 (Rosedale; Lady Jarvis gives table; Sarah and Mrs Fairburn scenes; George goes back to London).
- Jan 2 1911: Mellor receives Dante in white vellum from Mrs H.
- Apr 12–16: Riley at Easter; Holy Week; Blessing of Font at Westminster Cathedral; Maeterlinck remark; Housman "did not go to Florence after all."
- May 1: Housman laid up with pneumonia (Hendon). May 4: worse; Mrs H telegraphed. May 5: Mrs H arrives. May 8–15: Mrs H nursing day and night; "weak heart."
- May 20: Mellor visits Housman (likes visitors); Mrs H tired.
- June 10: Housmans to Brighton.
- May 22 C. letter: Elsie and Jack to London; Copenhagen.
- June 10 C. letter (Rosedale): Mrs H "fearfully ill"; Lady Jarvis's musical party.
- June 26 C. letter: Oakley (Randall, Fairburn); Housman hired steam yacht; Mrs H to Ireland (west coast) with Lady Jarvis; "won't think of divorcing."
- June 27–July 2 Mellor: Housman invites him to Oakley (A. also); A. declines; Solway's concert (July 1; Mrs H drives Mellor to Hendon); Mrs H to Ireland; July 2: Fairburn and C-S at Oakley.
- Oct 28 1911: Mrs H back from Ireland (Sunday in London; Oakley Wednesday); Mellor visits; Oct 30: A. back from Scotland; C. back from Copenhagen.
- Nov 1: music hall with A. and C. Nov 2: Aunt Ruth on Copenhagen (Caryl; Edmund; Uncle Arthur: "would have got us into war with the Danes").
- Nov 3: Mellor dines with A.; Nov 4: Rosedale party (A., C., Mellor? , Mrs Vaughan).
- Nov 6: Mrs H to Folkestone (with Miss Housman); Housman and sister quarrelled.
- Nov 25: Oakley (Lady Jarvis, A., C-S); Housman to Paris.
- Nov 27: play (farce); Mellor to remain in London (Riley at Christmas).
- Nov 28: Mrs H back to Folkestone till Christmas; A. abroad at Christmas.
- Dec 20: A. to Paris; C. to spend Christmas at Oakley.

**The Death (Dec 21–22, 1911)**
- C. letter (Dec 22, Halkin St): Thursday luncheon with George (going to Paris night train, "tired of England"); C. to Oakley; butler; Mrs H gone to London (Garland's Hotel); Housman arrives 4:45 with C-S; hands C. a letter from Mrs H; Housman reads it through twice, tears, burns; "We will go"; collapses; C-S telephones; Australian doctor: heart failure; Mrs H and Miss H arrive around six; Mrs H "almost frighteningly calm"; C. sends George a telegram.
- Mellor diary (Dec 22): Cunninghame rang him (Housman died suddenly). Mellor's guilt: Housman's telegram from Mrs H ("Albert dangerously ill. Fear worst. Cannot come. Clare") was opened by Mellor at the office, forwarded to Hôtel Meurice; A. had left office after 5 pm, dining at a club, meeting servant at station; A. had said "don't forward telegrams till I see them."
- C. letter (Rosedale, Dec 22): Lady Jarvis; Mrs H went to Garland's Hotel often; Mrs Fairburn scenes; "shatter him."
- Jan 1 1912 C. letter: funeral Tuesday; Mrs H to Rosedale; Florence; George back; Housman "left everything to her." P.S.: Mellor said "nothing."

**1912**
- Jan 1 1912: A. thanks Mellor; "Everything was quite right"; doesn't mention Mrs H.
- Feb 28 1912: Mrs H to Mellor: entered Convent of the Presentation; intends to be nun.
- Feb 28 C. letter: "rather *selfish*"; Dr Johnson "fear of vice"; "positively *wicked*"; George "life destroyed."
- Mar 1 1912: Mellor dines with C.; C. asks rules of leaving convent; Mellor writes Father Stanway.
- Mar 2: Stanway telegram; Mar 4: lunch at Club; Kensington Gardens walk. Info: six months' postulancy; two years' "Habit and White Veil"; three years' simple vows; solemn perpetual vows. Mellor's hypothetical case (X., Mrs X., Y.); Stanway's argument: vocation, "categorical imperative"; "marrying Christ"; "In la sua volontate e nostra pace"; "a tiny accident… a nerve snap"; "a long stress pushed a soul out of its real shape."
- Mar 7 Mellor reports to C.; C. "They never do let people go."
- Mar 7 C. letter: George "reprieve" vs "respite" (Mar 12 letter).
- Aug 10 1912 C. letter (London): Lady Jarvis at Rosedale; Mrs H novice; taken veil; "for all intents and purposes" irrevocable; George goes to Ireland with sister; C.: "wicked mistake," "selfish"; George: "priests… regular conspiracy" (C. thinks a mask).
- Aug 19 1912 Mellor at Rosedale: Lady Jarvis: "the person concerned is the only judge"; "I understand it and approve of it"; "Clare knew you would understand, even if you didn't understand."
- Aug 26 1912 Mellor at Carbis Bay Hotel alone; Father Stanway preaches; Mellor re-reads *Les Misérables* from beginning.
- Aug 27: Stanway leaves two quotes on card, both from Thomas à Kempis: "By so much the more does a man draw nigh to God as he goes away from all earthly solace"; "Whosoever is not ready to suffer all things and to stand resigned to the will of his beloved is not worthy to be called a lover."
- Aug 28 1912: Mellor resolves to give up keeping diary (last entry).

## NOTABLE DATE/TEXT QUIRKS
- Diary has some date errors (e.g., "Tuesday, June 12th" after "Monday June 13"; "Friday July 3rd" in June section; "Monday October 3rd" in 1911 section is actually 1911; "Tuesday, January 3rd" 1911 no weekday match; "Tuesday April 12th" 1911).
- Some dates ambiguous with missing year (Oct 3 1910 vs 1911).
- Riley: "Hôtel Meurice" forwarding; Mellor's aunt is Lady Mellor (Mar 1 1910 "my aunt Lady Mellor").
